description:
What this shows: Consensus proposals and validations received from peers, and transaction relay efficiency for this node.
Use it to: Check that peers are feeding this node proposals, validations, and transactions, and gauge relay overhead.

panels.title: Peer Proposal Receive Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How many consensus proposals this node receives from peers per second.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of received proposals over 5 minutes, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*A steady rate roughly proportional to the number of proposing validators.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; scales with validator count and connectivity.*

###### Watch for:
*A drop toward zero (isolation from the network) or a sudden flood far above baseline (proposal spam).*

###### Source:
[PeerImp.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp)

###### Function:
`PeerImp::onMessage(TMProposeSet)`

targets.expr: label_replace(sum by (service_instance_id, xrpl_branch, xrpl_node_role) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", xrpl_work_item=~"$xrpl_work_item", xrpl_branch=~"$xrpl_branch", xrpl_node_role=~"$xrpl_node_role", span_name="peer.proposal.receive"}[$__rate_interval])), "series", "Proposals Received / Sec", "", "")

panels.title: Peer Validation Receive Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How many ledger validations this node receives from peers per second.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of received validations over 5 minutes, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Steady and proportional to the number of validators the node hears from.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; roughly one burst per validator per closed ledger.*

###### Watch for:
*A fall toward zero (loss of validator connectivity) or an abnormal surge from untrusted sources.*

###### Source:
[PeerImp.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp)

###### Function:
`PeerImp::onMessage(TMValidation)`

targets.expr: label_replace(sum by (service_instance_id, xrpl_branch, xrpl_node_role) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", xrpl_work_item=~"$xrpl_work_item", xrpl_branch=~"$xrpl_branch", xrpl_node_role=~"$xrpl_node_role", span_name="peer.validation.receive"}[$__rate_interval])), "series", "Validations Received / Sec", "", "")

panels.title: Proposals Trusted vs Untrusted
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The share of received proposals that come from trusted (UNL) validators versus everyone else.*

###### How it's computed:
*Received-proposal rate split by trust status over 5 minutes, shown as proportions.*

###### Reading it:
*A healthy node with a good UNL shows a solid trusted slice.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; a meaningful trusted fraction is expected.*

###### Watch for:
*A collapsing trusted share or a large untrusted volume, consistent with proposal flooding from non-UNL peers.*

###### Source:
[PeerImp.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp)

###### Function:
`PeerImp::onMessage(TMProposeSet)`

targets.expr: label_replace(sum by (proposal_trusted, service_instance_id, xrpl_branch, xrpl_node_role) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", xrpl_work_item=~"$xrpl_work_item", xrpl_branch=~"$xrpl_branch", xrpl_node_role=~"$xrpl_node_role", proposal_trusted=~"$proposal_trusted", span_name="peer.proposal.receive"}[$__rate_interval])), "series", "Trusted = $1", "proposal_trusted", "(.*)")

panels.title: Validations Trusted vs Untrusted
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The share of received validations from trusted (UNL) validators versus untrusted sources.*

###### How it's computed:
*Received-validation rate split by trust status over 5 minutes, shown as proportions.*

###### Reading it:
*The trusted slice should dominate for a well-configured node.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; trusted validations expected to be the majority.*

###### Watch for:
*A shrinking trusted share or a spike of untrusted validations, which can indicate misconfiguration or abuse.*

###### Source:
[PeerImp.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp)

###### Function:
`PeerImp::onMessage(TMValidation)`

panels.title: Reduce-Relay Peer Selection
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How transaction relay picks peers: chosen relay sources, suppressed peers, and peers with the feature off.*

###### How it's computed:
*Current peer counts in each category (selected, suppressed, not-enabled), per node.*

###### Reading it:
*A high suppressed-to-selected ratio means relay is saving bandwidth as intended.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; suppressed should exceed selected in a well-connected mesh.*

###### Watch for:
*A large not-enabled count (older peers forcing full relay) or selected climbing while suppressed falls.*

###### Source:
[MetricsRegistry.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp)

###### Function:
`registerReduceRelayGauge`

targets.expr: label_replace(reduce_relay_metrics{metric="not_enabled_peers",service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", xrpl_work_item=~"$xrpl_work_item", xrpl_branch=~"$xrpl_branch", xrpl_node_role=~"$xrpl_node_role"}, "series", "Not Enabled", "", "")

panels.title: Reduce-Relay Missing-Tx Frequency
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How often a peer has to fetch a transaction it missed because relay suppressed it.*

###### How it's computed:
*The reported frequency of on-demand missing-transaction fetches, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; near-flat means suppression is well tuned.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; a low, stable value is expected.*

###### Watch for:
*A rising trend, meaning suppression is too aggressive and the on-demand fetch path is growing.*

###### Source:
[MetricsRegistry.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp)

###### Function:
`registerReduceRelayGauge`

targets.expr: label_replace(reduce_relay_metrics{metric="missing_tx_freq",service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", xrpl_work_item=~"$xrpl_work_item", xrpl_branch=~"$xrpl_branch", xrpl_node_role=~"$xrpl_node_role"}, "series", "Missing Tx Freq", "", "")
